note.headline: 🟢 Tier fits
note.text: Small team of 49 employees (pitchbook.com) and $44M total raised (pitchbook.com) support the current tier. The evidence is mixed: check whether the $30M Series B (en.wikipedia.org) is raising travel spend.

reasons: No flags - research is consistent with Tier 2.
notes: Verified funding: $30M Series B led by Accel (en.wikipedia.org); $12M Series A (venturebeat.com); $44M total raised (pitchbook.com).
No employee data found - no reason to change the tier.

ai.reason: The declared $168,000 GBV falls in the Tier 2 band ($100K-$500K), and PitchBook's 49-employee count is below the 150-employee threshold for Tier 2 by headcount, so the current tier matches the numbers. The $12M Series A (January 2024) and $30M Series B (May 2025) are a fast funding path that could mean growing travel spend, but the Series B is about 18 months old and no source shows travel spend above the Tier 2 band, so this is a minor concern to glance at rather than evidence the tier is wrong.
